target_customer: Latin American banks, fintech lenders, insurers and other companies that need legally valid e-signatures with identity verification.
problem: Signing contracts in Latin America typically needs a notary or in person identity checks, which slows lending, hiring and commercial deals.
business_model: B2B SaaS and API priced per transaction for e-signatures and identity verification.

founders.name: Manuel Olguin
previous_startups: Cinepapaya (acquired by NBC Universal through Fandango Media, 2016)
founders.background_notes: YC page: led Cinepapaya for four years and expanded it to 12 countries and about 80 percent of the region's theaters.

founders.background_notes: YC page: designed and implemented the Cinepapaya platform.

founders.background_notes: Named a co-founder by the YC page and the Magma Partners announcement; no bio.

founders.background_notes: Named a co-founder by the YC page and the Magma Partners announcement; no bio.

technical_complexity.rationale: Video signatures, matching to official records and social profiles, and blockchain notarization are integration heavy, with liveness and biometrics later; the hardest part was legal validity across countries.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations with lenders and reusable verified identities create switching costs, but global e-signature vendors and local identity providers could compete.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows a global vendor absorbing Keynua; it reports nearly 500 clients and over 2 million transactions in 2023 (Gestion, April 2024).

market_need_then: Magma Partners says the goal was a regional platform to verify identity and validate transactions without a notary, which would streamline Latin American business processes; Olguin's own frustration with signing at Cinepapaya is reported as the origin.

branding.domain_note: Uses keynua.com. A US trademark filing for KEYNUA is dated December 10, 2018 per a trademark record in search results.

identity.voice_and_tone: Product focused, tagline 'The signature with identity' on its site.

branding.brand_signature: The 'signature with identity' framing and short video signature.

brand_strength.rationale: Customers include Telefonica, Belcorp and Pago Efectivo per its site, but no independent press on the brand and an unusual name with unknown meaning.

outcome_analysis: Keynua is an active, small company (15 people) run by founders who previously sold Cinepapaya to Fandango. It raised small undisclosed checks from Nilo Ventures and Magma Partners in March 2019, launched its product in 2020 and by 2023 reports nearly 500 clients and over 2 million transactions, planning to enter Argentina in 2024. Funding after 2019 was not found, so growth appears capital light, but scale is modest.
notes: Gestion (April 2024) says Keynua got US$2 million from Y Combinator in 2019, which conflicts with aggregator totals ($1.4M Latka, $1.76M in another listing); not recorded as a round. The Nilo Ventures Medium post returned 403; Nilo's round is from Contxto and LAVCA snippets and some sources date it April 2019. Founder education not found; Magma's page links Olguin to Canadas' LinkedIn so names are as given by the YC page. Competitors: no source dated near 2019 naming rivals was found; the Magma post, Gestion and the site name none. Added the YC investment of US$150 thousand: Contxto (2019-04-06) reports it 'according to Crunchbase'; month not given, so dated 2019. Nilo and Magma: Contxto (2019-04-06) says the Nilo round closed 'last month' and the Magma post is dated 2019-03-19; neither source mentions the other investor or states a round label or amount, so it is unconfirmed whether they are one round or two. They stay as two entries with stage other because no source labels either one seed.
